stock.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on free cash flow yield, valuation against its own industry, earnings yield — revenue +8.2% over the trailing year, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

stock.counterargument: Growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +7.2%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $116.86 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-07-31, 87 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-07-31, 87 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-26.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-12-03) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

sources.fundamentals: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (twelve quarters), point-in-time by accepted timestamp, topped up from companyfacts for companies that have filed since the newest data set

NBC News spoke to “several industry leaders, consultants, and investigators advising law enforcement” offices probing the biggest thefts yet and reported that since June, thieves have “made away with more than $100 million in data center freight.”

stories.title: Kevin Roose is AGI-pilled. Why aren’t you?
stories.excerpt: Today, I’m talking to Kevin Roose, journalist and author of the new book The AGI Chronicles, which details the recent and explosive transformation of the AI industry. Kevin was a longtime New York Times reporter and host of the popular podcast Hard Fork, but he and friend of the show Casey Newton…
stories.lead:
Kevin was a longtime New York Times reporter and host of the popular podcast Hard Fork, but he and friend of the show Casey Newton just left the Times to start the all-new tech podcast Machine Gods, which launched last week.

Kevin and I talked about launching Machine Gods and what it’s like to go from The New York Times to being an independent creator — and then of course we talked about the book, which is an excellently reported dive into the companies racing to build artificial general intelligence.

stories.title: A Practical Introduction to Web Scraping in Python
stories.excerpt: Get started with Python web scraping: parse data from websites and interact with HTML forms using Beautiful Soup and MechanicalSoup.
stories.lead:
Python web scraping allows you to collect and parse data from websites programmatically. With powerful libraries like urllib, Beautiful Soup, and MechanicalSoup, you can fetch and manipulate HTML content effortlessly. By automating data collection tasks, Python makes web scraping both efficient and effective.

By the end of this tutorial, you’ll understand that:

This tutorial guides you through extracting data from websites using string methods, regular expressions, and HTML parsers.

stories.title: Quiz: Working With APIs in Python: Reading Public Data
stories.excerpt: Test your understanding of consuming REST APIs with Requests, from status codes and JSON to query parameters, authentication, and rate limits.
stories.lead:
In this quiz, you’ll test your understanding of Working With APIs in Python: Reading Public Data.

By working through this quiz, you’ll revisit how requests and responses work, what common status codes mean, how to read JSON data, how to filter results with query parameters, and how to authenticate with an API key.

You’ll also check how to go easy on an API’s servers with pagination and by respecting rate limits. Once you know these basics, you can start pulling data from almost any public API into your own projects.

stories.title: 'The stakes are existential!': Thousands of Israelis living abroad return home to vote in October 27 elections
stories.excerpt: Because Israel does not allow citizens to vote remotely, including at embassies, many expatriates have flown home to vote. Turnout appears particularly high among opponents of Benjamin Netanyahu, who have traveled from New York, Washington, Paris, London, Madrid and even Australia.

stories.title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
stories.excerpt: Mississippi has the largest proportional Black population in the country. It's one reason the U.S. Senate race has seen millions in last-minute spending and high-profile campaign visits.
stories.lead:
COLUMBUS, Miss. — On paper, Mississippi's U.S. Senate race seems like the perfect place for a political upset this year, an assertion President Trump's Monday rally there seems to support.

It has the highest share of Black voters in the country, at close to 40%. It's a rural, agriculture-heavy state that is also among the poorest, so higher prices are felt harder.

But President Trump won the state by 23 points in 2024, and it's extremely racially polarized, meaning not enough white voters back Democrats for the party to win statewide.

stories.title: Truce begins in Ukraine city where residents ate weeds to survive
stories.excerpt: The ceasefire in Oleshky, secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and the evacuation of civilians.
stories.lead:
A truce has begun in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where residents have been trapped without food, water and electricity.

Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry say the limited ceasefire is being respected. The truce, which the White House said was secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuation on Friday.

Oleshky, along the front line in the Kherson region, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River, which separates it from Ukrainian positions, and on the other by Russian forces.

stories.title: Harry Kane becomes first Englishman in 25 years to win Ballon d'Or
stories.excerpt: Kane was followed in the voting by Kylian Mbappé. Spain star Alexia Putellas won her third women's Ballon d'Or. Outside, fans packed the streets and climbed light poles near the London Palladium.
stories.lead:
LONDON — Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or on Monday thanks to his prolific scoring last season.

Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last campaign — he was Europe's top scorer — and smashed scoring records in Germany for Bayern Munich and at the World Cup, where he captained England to a third-place finish.

The 33-year-old Kane says winning the prestigious individual award was built on so much more.

stories.title: Why it could take time for a new Israeli government to form
stories.excerpt: Israel faces what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history.
stories.lead:
Israelis are voting in what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history.

It is the first parliamentary election since the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks and subsequent conflicts across the region - in Gaza, Iran, Lebanon, Syria and Yemen.

BBC Middle East correspondent Yolande Knell explains why it may take some time before a new government is formed after the polls close.

stories.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
stories.excerpt: The prediction market has hired a former FBI official to make sure political insiders don't use the platform for profit from confidential election information.
stories.lead:
Polymarket has investigated "dozens" of bets on its prediction markets related to the midterm election, according to the company's head of global intelligence and investigations, Shana Bautista.

At least two of these Polymarket investigations have been referred to its regulator, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, according to a person who is familiar with the probes, but not authorized to speak publicly about them.

stories.title: Budget measures to include fuel duty freeze and food tariff cuts
stories.excerpt: The BBC understands the government will also freeze fuel duty again in the Budget.
stories.lead:
Making higher tax-free mileage rates permanent and the removal of import taxes on some food items are among the measures being announced ahead of Wednesday's Budget.

The series of small announcements are part of Chancellor John Healey's pledge to give families what he is calling "breathing space" with the cost of living.

The ‘Footsie’ is down 108 points, or 1%, at 10,659…
stories.lead:
Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets and the world economy.

As he puts the finishing touches to tomorrow’s budget, John Healey may note that another bank has reported a jump in earnings.

HSBC is handing $2.7bn (£2bn) to shareholders after a 32% surge in profits, that will further assure the Treasury that the UK’s top banks can shoulder a tax hike in the budget, my colleague Kalyeena Makortoff reports.

stories.title: 'I'm a single mum on £41,000 and limit my weekly shop to £40.' What do you want from the Budget?
stories.excerpt: People earning from £380 a month to £150,000 a year tell the BBC what they want to see in this year's Budget.
stories.lead:
Chloe, Emily and Robert all spoke to the BBC about what they would like to see in the Budget

Chancellor John Healey is set to unveil his first Budget on Wednesday.

Unlike in previous years there have been very few leaks about what will be in it, though Healey's tax and spending plans will be under close scrutiny at a time when government borrowing costs are at "historic highs".

stories.title: Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many
stories.excerpt: Democrats hold significant advantages going into Election Day, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. But lagging enthusiasm among key groups is just one indicator that gains may not come easy.
stories.lead:
📲 Get the latest on the midterms & more in the NPR App

Democrats retain significant midterm electoral advantages, with key data pointing to them being the favorites to win control of the U.S. House. But, there are indications of why a potential wave could be limited, a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds.

The poll also sheds light on the issues driving voters across the ideological spectrum. The cost of living continues to be top of mind overall with a third of people saying they've experienced financial hardship in the past year and 4 in 10 saying their personal finances have gotten worse.
